compiled_state.description:
# Six tickets carry a FORCE_CLOSE audit record AND a certified completion attestation

## Observation, NOT a diagnosis

Found while verifying that bug 738a's fix does not make a force-close signable (it does not — that
guard runs first and is now mutation-checked). Scanning the whole store for force-close audit records
turned up a population I could not fully explain, so it is filed rather than folded into 738a.

```
tickets carrying a FORCE_CLOSE audit record:  146
of those, completion-verifier == certified:     6
   119f (epic)   145e (story)  93d0 (story)
   9447 (story)  e879 (story)  e95e (story)
```

All six are epics/stories, not bugs, and none carries a `close_class`. **No force-closed BUG is
certified**, which is why this did not surface through 738a's own investigation.

## Why this may well be benign

A `FORCE_CLOSE` comment is a permanent audit record; it does not disappear when a ticket is later
re-closed properly. So "has a force-close record AND is certified" is consistent with the documented
remedy having been applied. Five of the six were signed AFTER their last force-close:

```
119f  signed 1785223166  last force 1785223127   signature AFTER force
145e  signed 1784801284  last force 1784795114   signature AFTER force
93d0  signed 1785268444  last force 1785268436   signature AFTER force
9447  signed 1785221502  last force 1785219250   signature AFTER force
e879  signed 1785665032  last force 1785625021   signature AFTER force
e95e  signed 1784248078  last force 1784346923   signature BEFORE force
```

**But none of them records `last_reopened_at`**, and the documented remedy is reopen → in_progress →
re-close. A signature appearing after a force-close *without* a reopen needs an explanation.

## The leading candidate, explicitly UNVERIFIED

`sign_completion_verdict`'s docstring names a SECOND producer: "the trusted op-cert gate service's
worker on a PASS verdict", which points `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` / `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` at the
provisioned environment key and calls the same seam. That service can mint a completion cert
independently of the close path, which would explain a signature landing after a force-close with no
reopen — and would be entirely correct behaviour.

**I have not traced any of the six to that service.** Do not treat the above as diagnosed; it is the
hypothesis a reader should test first.

## `e95e` is the odd one out

Its signature PREDATES its last force-close by ~28 hours. So whatever certifies it today was minted
before the force-close, not after. That ordering is not explained by the op-cert-service hypothesis
and is the most interesting single case here.

## Why it matters even if benign

`child_closure_findings` treats a valid completion attestation as sufficient for a child's closure to
count as certified. If any of these six is a direct child of a parent that later closed, that parent's
certification rested on an attestation whose provenance relative to a force-close is unclear. Worth
settling, because the whole point of the attestation chain is that certification propagates only from
verified state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] each of the six is traced to the producer that minted its attestation (close path vs the trusted
      op-cert gate service), with the evidence recorded here
- [ ] `e95e`'s signature-before-force-close ordering is explained, or confirmed as a defect
- [ ] it is determined whether any of the six is a direct child whose parent's certification depended
      on it, and if so whether that parent's signature should stand
- [ ] if the op-cert service can mint a completion cert for a ticket whose close was FORCED, a
      decision is recorded on whether that is intended

## Method note

Three scans returned wrong answers before this one: two pointed at a tracker copy that had none of
these records, and a third used `subprocess` `grep`, which disagreed with the shell's `grep` (193
matching files vs 0). Only the pure-Python scan is trustworthy, and the numbers above come from it.
An empty result from a scan is not evidence of absence until the scan itself is verified.
